newsitem.title: USA: Lunar stock down as sales outlook offered.
newsitem.headline: Lunar stock down as sales outlook offered.

text.p: Lunar Corp shares dropped more than 46 percent Monday after the company said it did not expect significant sales of its new bone densitometer immediately after it brings the product to market in fiscal 1998.
"Our new product measures bone density, and we expect to start selling it in the next fiscal year" beginning July 1, Robert Beckman, Lunar's chief financial officer, told Reuters.
However, Lunar said it did not expect substantial sales in the immediate future. Beckman declined to say what the company expects in terms of sales volume.
Lunar stock, which fell as much as 11 during the session, was down 10-1/4 at 19 during midafternoon.

Lunar announced its PIXI bone densitometer in early April. The product uses a dual-energy X-ray to estimate bone mineral density in the heel and forearm. PIXI measurements take only five seconds, which is 60 times faster than conventional peripheral densitometers, Lunar said.

Lunar, which makes a range of devices for the diagnosis and monitoring of osteoporosis and other diseases, said it recently gained the approval of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market the product.
"I really don't understand the decline in the stock price," he said.
Analysts were not immediately available to comment on the Lunar stock decline.
